stimuli.text:
Scenario 1

Imagine you are traveling very far away, and meet a new group of people you know nothing about. You are trying to learn about the people, the society, and the language all at the same time.

There are two people in this group, whose names are Paji and Tudo. Paji has more power and influence than Tudo does.

There's an action in this society which is called daxing. You hear that daxing is very rare, almost no one ever daxes. Daxing is very harmful to other people.

People in this society have something they call 'jats', which really matter to them.

One day you see that Paji catches Tudo daxing. Paji could either do nothing, take away half of Tudo's jats, or take away all of Tudo's jats.

If Paji takes away Tudo's jats, Paji will lose a large amount of their own jats as well. Doing nothing has no direct costs or benefits for Paji.

queries.prompt: In general, how much does Paji care about justice and acting fairly?
How strongly is Paji biased in favor or against Tudo, relative to other people in the society?
How much more does Paji care about their own direct costs and benefits, relative to other people in the society?
In this society, how morally wrong is daxing?
